tldr: This was an in-person technical interview of a back-end candidate (referred to as Zarek, a C# engineer ex-PDI/Maintel), run by Harry's team.
Topics covered: data validation, shared contracts, retries, slow queries, production incidents, testing, a code read of a pub/sub handler, and a whiteboard design for a carrier proxy API.
The candidate gave sound answers on validation, retry limits and rate limiting, and spotted the main code bugs. They were weaker on contract testing and had no pub/sub experience.
The candidate met Dan and John, was asked about office days and release practice, then was shown round the office.
Afterwards the panel's view was that it went well and they got a decent feel for the candidate. No formal decision was recorded.
questions: Whether to progress the candidate. The panel only said it should be good and no hiring decision was recorded.
Whether the code-read exercise should be reworked. Room 1 said it was left Fuse-adjacent and could be replaced with a native example.
What the roughly fifty Windows services on the legacy app servers actually do. This was raised only as an aside.
